draft.title: Genetic drift
card: Genetic drift is a change in allele frequencies from one generation to the next that happens by chance. It is not caused by an allele helping an organism survive.

Drift is strongest in small populations. With few individuals, chance events can easily make an allele more or less common, or remove it entirely. In a large population, chance averages out and has little effect.
a disaster such as a fire or flood kills many individuals at random. The few survivors carry only some of the alleles, so the population has different allele frequencies and less variation.
a few individuals leave a population and start a new one. The new population has only the alleles those founders carried, so its allele frequencies can differ from the original.
draft.remember: Drift is change by chance, and it has the biggest effect when a population is small.

a.q: Which statement best describes genetic drift?
opts: A chance change in allele frequencies between generations
A rise in alleles that give a survival advantage
A shift in allele frequencies caused by migrating adults
A new allele appearing when DNA is copied incorrectly
a.why: Drift is a change in allele frequencies that happens by chance. The option about a survival advantage describes natural selection, where the change is not random with respect to the environment.
a.clue: Think about what causes the change: chance or advantage?

b.q: A storm kills most of an island's lizards at random. The survivors happen to carry mostly the allele for brown skin, which was rare before. Why did brown skin become common?
opts: Chance left mostly brown carriers in a small population
Brown skin gave the lizards an advantage in the storm
The storm caused a mutation that created brown skin
Brown lizards arrived from another island and bred
b.why: The storm killed at random, so survival did not depend on skin colour. The survivors were few, and chance made brown alleles common, which is the bottleneck effect. Natural selection is the tempting answer, but the deaths were random.
b.clue: Did skin colour decide who survived the storm?

a.best: A chance change in allele frequencies between generations

b.best: Chance left mostly brown carriers in a small population
